description: Held-out governing-rules set (#2024): a fictional clinic network's patient records and clinical safety standard (40 atomic obligations) and analyst-worded requirements, labelled blind to every arm's prompt by two independent labellers with adjudicated disagreements. Read it only for a decision, never to tune a prompt.

contentHash.covers: sha256 of the JSON of [policy, rules, items, each revision's text with LF line endings]; ANNOTATION.md, the labelling files and the thresholds are outside it

policy.title: Kestrel Vale Health Partners — Patient Records and Clinical Safety Standard

annotation.labelledBy: two independent AI labellers (claude-opus-5-5), adjudicated by a third pass; not a person
annotation.procedure: Written for this set in original wording by an agent that read no governing prompt, arm or baseline; labelled against policy-v1 by that agent and, blind to its labels, by a second agent given only the policy and the requirements; each disagreement settled by a third pass with a written reason. No arm has run on it. See ANNOTATION.md and labelling/.

rules.summary: Confirm full name and date of birth before opening a present patient's chart.
Merging two charts needs two staff confirmations and stays reversible for ninety days.
Video and phone consultations start with a one-time code to the mobile on file.
Preferred names are allowed, but the legal name stays and goes on prescriptions and referrals.
Newborn charts get a temporary identifier, replaced by the national number within fourteen days.
Clinicians open a chart only when involved in the patient's care, apart from recorded emergency access.
Access without a care relationship needs a typed reason first and privacy-officer review within five working days.
Reception and billing see contact, appointment and payment details, never clinical content.
Staff-patient and public-figure charts are restricted; each opening is reported the same day.
Consulting-room computers lock after five idle minutes.
Patient information leaves the network only with recorded consent or a legal requirement.
Consent withdrawal takes effect for disclosures from one working day after receipt.
Consent to text or email contact is recorded separately from consent to treatment.
No disclosure to parents about 16- and 17-year-olds without their agreement, barring safeguarding.
Research use needs ethics approval and removal of names, addresses and health numbers.
Prescriptions are checked against recorded allergies; an override needs the prescriber's reason.
Controlled drugs need matching prescribing authority and a register entry.
Repeat prescriptions are reviewed by a clinician at least every twelve months.
Children's doses use a weight taken within thirty days.
Medicine warnings can be acknowledged per prescription, never turned off.
Results reach the portal only after the ordering clinician's review, unless routine and normal.
Messages to patients carry only time and place unless they opted into detail.
Appointment reminders go at least forty-eight hours ahead.
Every letter and message sent to a patient is copied to their chart.
Consent talks in another language need a qualified interpreter, never relatives.
Adult charts are kept eight years after last contact.
Children's charts are kept to age twenty-five, or eight years after death if sooner.
Clinical entries are never deleted; corrections are new entries showing the original, who and why.
Requests for a copy of one's own chart are answered within thirty days.
Scanned paper is checked for legibility and kept three months before shredding.
Harm and near-miss events are reported within twenty-four hours.
A harmed patient is told what happened by a senior clinician within ten working days.
Clinical software faults that affected care are reported to the clinical safety officer.
Changes to what clinicians see or the order of clinical steps are safety-assessed and logged before release.
Suspected loss or disclosure of patient information is reported to the privacy officer within four hours.
A supplier signs a data processing agreement before receiving patient information.
Patient information is stored only in in-country data centres.
Medical devices are inventoried with owner and software version before connecting.
Clinical laptops, tablets and phones are encrypted and remotely wipeable.
No removable media for patient information, except desk-issued encrypted drives.

items.title: Give covering doctors the full list
items.text: Doctors covering a shift should be able to pull up the notes of anyone registered at the practice, not just today's bookings, in case someone rings in.

applies.businessFact: Will covering doctors open only the notes of people they are seeing or acting for, apart from a recorded emergency access?
Will a covering doctor have to type a reason before opening the notes of someone not booked today, with each such opening reviewed by the privacy officer within five working days?

items.title: Move bookings to the cheapest cloud region
items.text: Move the appointment system to our hosting supplier's cheapest cloud region, which is currently overseas.

applies.businessFact: Do we have a signed data processing agreement with the hosting supplier?

items.title: Dark mode for the staff intranet
items.text: Add a dark colour scheme to the staff intranet, switchable from the page header.

items.title: Check two details before opening someone's file
items.text: When someone arrives at the minor injuries unit, the triage nurse asks for their full name and their date of birth, and opens the chart only once both match.

items.title: Paediatric syrup calculator
items.text: When a GP prescribes a syrup for a toddler, the screen suggests the millilitres per kilo from the latest figure on the growth chart.

applies.businessFact: Will the calculator refuse a growth-chart figure that is more than thirty days old?
Has the clinical safety officer assessed the calculator before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Results straight to the app
items.text: Lab results appear in the patient app the moment the laboratory sends them, so people are not left waiting for a call.

items.title: Tidy up duplicate registrations
items.text: A single front-desk user can fold two registrations for one individual into a single entry when they notice a duplicate while searching, with no second check.

items.title: Asthma extract for the university study
items.text: Send the university's respiratory team a spreadsheet of every asthma patient with their name, home address, age and inhaler use, for a study our ethics committee approved last month.

applies.businessFact: Have the patients in the extract consented to their details going to the university?

items.title: Keep GPs signed in for the whole surgery
items.text: GPs find it slow to sign back in between each person they see, so the desktop should stay open and ready for the entire morning or afternoon session.

items.title: Parking details on the clinic finder
items.text: Show the nearest car park and its charges on each clinic's page of the public website.

items.title: Video appointments from home
items.text: Let people book a video appointment with their GP and join it from the link in their booking confirmation, without travelling to the clinic.

applies.businessFact: Will the GP confirm who they are speaking to at the start of each call, with a one-time code sent to the mobile number on the chart?
Is a copy of each booking confirmation sent to the patient saved on their chart?

items.title: Stop nagging GPs about combinations they already know
items.text: A GP who keeps seeing the same interaction pop-up for a long-standing combination can tick 'don't remind me again' for that person.

applies.businessFact: Has the clinical safety officer assessed the 'don't remind me again' option before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: One tick box at registration
items.text: The new registration form has a single tick box reading 'I agree to treatment and to be contacted by email and text'.

items.title: Mums and dads can follow their kids' bookings
items.text: The family account in the app lists every booking and test outcome for each child linked to it, up to the age of eighteen.

applies.businessFact: Are results shown in the family account only after the clinician who ordered them has reviewed them?

items.title: Faster prescribing in the minor injuries unit
items.text: Nurse prescribers in the minor injuries unit can skip the allergy screen with one click when the queue is long.

applies.businessFact: Has the clinical safety officer assessed the one-click skip of the allergy screen before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Clear the post room the same day
items.text: Once incoming hospital letters have been photographed into the system, the admin team bin the originals that afternoon to free up space.

items.title: New brand colours on the website
items.text: Update the public website's buttons, fonts and logo to the network's new brand guidelines.

items.title: Emergency access to notes outside your list
items.text: A clinician who opens the notes of someone they are not treating must first type why; the privacy officer then gets each such case to review, and must close it within five working days.

applies.businessFact: Has the clinical safety officer assessed the new reason prompt and review step before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Say why they are coming in the SMS nudge
items.text: The SMS sent the day before should say what the visit is for, such as 'your diabetes review' or 'your smear test', so fewer people forget.

applies.businessFact: Is a copy of each SMS reminder sent to patients saved on their chart?

items.title: Two-year repeats for blood pressure tablets
items.text: People on long-term blood pressure tablets get a repeat that runs for two years, so they do not have to book a medication review every year.

items.title: Use the name people prefer everywhere
items.text: Print the name a patient likes to be called on everything we produce for them, prescriptions and hospital referral letters included.

items.title: Replacing a lost work phone
items.text: If a clinician loses their work phone, they tell the IT desk on the next working day so a replacement can be ordered.

applies.businessFact: Do the network's work phones encrypt their storage and can the IT desk wipe a lost one remotely?

items.title: A son or daughter translates before a minor operation
items.text: When the person only speaks Polish, their son or daughter can translate the risks of a minor operation and sign the form alongside them.

items.title: Bank holiday opening hours
items.text: Let clinic managers enter bank holiday opening hours, which then appear on the public website's clinic pages.

items.title: Keep the history when a note is corrected
items.text: When a clinician corrects a consultation note, the system keeps the original wording alongside the new version, records who made the change and asks them for a reason.

applies.businessFact: Has the clinical safety officer assessed the new correction flow before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Connect the new ECG machine
items.text: Plug the new ECG machine in the treatment room into the network so traces go straight onto the chart.

applies.businessFact: Do we enter the ECG machine in the device inventory, with its owner and software version, before it is connected?
Has the clinical safety officer assessed the ECG traces appearing on the chart before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Clear out old adult charts
items.text: Delete adult charts automatically five years after the person's last visit, to cut storage costs.

items.title: Day list on a memory stick for the outreach van
items.text: The outreach nurses want to copy the day's visit list, with names, addresses and conditions, onto a memory stick so they can open it on the van's laptop where signal is poor.

applies.businessFact: Is the memory stick an encrypted drive issued by the IT service desk?
Is the van's laptop encrypted, and can it be wiped remotely?

items.title: Show reception the reason for the last visits
items.text: When someone checks in, show the receptionist their last three diagnoses so they can book the right length of follow-up appointment.

items.title: Canteen menu on the intranet
items.text: Publish the weekly staff canteen menu on the intranet home page.

items.title: Move the allergies panel to a tab
items.text: Move the allergies panel from the top of the consultation screen into a tab, to give clinicians more room for their notes.

applies.businessFact: Do we have the clinical safety officer's assessment of this change filed in the hazard log before it goes live?

items.title: Ask for your notes online
items.text: Patients can request their notes through the website, and the records team will post a printed copy within six weeks.

items.title: Email referral letters straight to patients
items.text: Letters made with the new referral template are emailed to the patient directly from the template tool, so they have the details of their referral before the hospital calls.

applies.businessFact: Is a copy of each emailed letter saved on the patient's chart?

items.title: Near-miss button on the prescribing screen
items.text: Add a 'report a near miss' button to the prescribing screen that saves a draft the pharmacist submits to the incident system at the end of each week.

applies.businessFact: Has the clinical safety officer assessed the new button before release, with the assessment filed in the hazard log?

items.title: Laptops for community nurses
items.text: Issue each community nurse a laptop whose disk is encrypted and which IT can erase remotely if it goes missing.

items.title: Reorder the website's frequently asked questions
items.text: Group the public website's frequently asked questions by topic and put the most-read ones first.
